en: They say that "bhaga" is a synonym for glory as seen in the treatises; because he is endowed with that glory in this world, the sage here is therefore "Bhagavān.
Or, [because he has] completely [destroyed the defilements], he is Bhagavān here; and for that reason, he is Bhagavān.
Or rather, he who is fortunate enough to be a recipient of worship is known here as "Bhagavat" because of that.
Just as those sages attained the auspicious goal, so too did he; therefore he is the Tathāgata.
Just as the seers followed the higher and the lower, so did he; therefore he is the Tathāgata.
Therefore, the Tathāgata spoke the truth; therefore, the Tathāgata went to existence;
or the Tathāgata has gone to peace, having gone such that he does not go again and again to renewed existence.

Having bound upon himself the impenetrable armor of forbearance and the mail of fortitude, which is as hard as resolve, that Sage struck down his enemies, such as Māra and the rest, with the bow of steadfastness;
and because of this, he, the Arhat, received worship from the world including its gods, humans, and nāgas.
Therefore, one who has destroyed the view of existence becomes a Vibhu, an Arhat.

Suffering, its cause, its cessation, and the path—because he has perfectly awakened to these entirely, and because it is possible to accomplish them and not otherwise, nor is it false; therefore he is the Perfectly Awakened One (Samyaksambuddha), and thus he is the Buddha upon the earth.
Since he possessed those three auspicious and rare knowledges, his conduct was indeed pure;
therefore, that best of sages became a self-existent one, endowed with both knowledge and conduct.
Because the Sage has comprehended the entirety of that which is to be known, he is the Sugata; or because he has personally realized the true path, he is the Sugata.
Out of compassion for all beings, [he provides] the refuge that is ageless, immortal, and fearless.
Or, because he proclaims the true Dharma, he is therefore called the Sugata.

He knows the world and the origin of the world, as well as the passing away of the world exactly as it is; and he has realized the path for the cessation of the world. Therefore, he is the Knower of the World, immeasurable.
Because he teaches well through equanimity, omniscience, and non-erroneousness, with an incomparable eye;
since there is no one equal to him, nor anyone superior, the Blessed One, the Great Sage, is unsurpassed.

Since he, the wise one of great compassion, has trained men for their welfare through purity and gentleness, he has led them away from the wrong path; therefore, this Great-Souled One is the Charioteer who tames those to be tamed among men.
Because he is omniscient, free from all defects, and the teacher of the supreme, unshakable Dharma;
and because his disciples shall thereby attain liberation, he is therefore the Teacher of gods and men.
That which has not been approached, that which is past, that which has been accepted, that which moves and does not move, and the entirety of the perishable and the imperishable—
since the Blessed One, honored by the wise, realized all this here at the foot of the Bodhi tree, he is therefore the Buddha.
